baseHeader.methodology: Source-linked original summaries and reference-guided educational reconstructions. Models and motion are unvalidated; artist titles do not independently verify taxonomy. Navigation groups are not a universal kingdom system. Microbial behavior depends on strain and conditions. Expansion entries are individually referenced authored morphology studies; legacy Protista/Monera reporting categories do not replace modern domains. Actual screenshots, software checks and draft status are distinct from independent scientific validation.

before.summary: A large raptor associated with water. Fish, carrion and other animal food contribute to its diet.

anatomy.name: Adult head, bill and eye
anatomy.description: White head and neck, pale yellow iris and a hooked yellow bill. Detailed credited artist geometry is retained; eye surfaces are added. Proportions remain unmeasured.

anatomy.name: Feet and talons
anatomy.description: Yellow bare lower legs and feet with dark hooked talons. A separate standing posture supports both feet; grasping, prey capture and landing remain unavailable.

anatomy.name: Flight feathers and white tail
anatomy.description: Dark brown wing and body feathers contrast with an adult white tail. The detailed source atlas is retained; pale wing bands are corrected to adult dark brown. Fine vane relief is authored; individual feather mechanics are not solved.

behaviors.label: Fly
behaviors.description: An eight-second display study moves paired arm and hand wings, with mild hand twist and tucked legs, then returns to extended wings. Authored joint angles and timing are uncalibrated.
behaviors.evidence: Species-level scientific context; authored exterior posture study
behaviors.timeScale: uncalibrated illustrative display seconds; no biological clock

behaviors.label: Standing
behaviors.description: Held adult standing posture using a separate credited folded-wing exterior, closed white tail and two feet. No compression of the flight mesh, head-turn cycle, landing or wing-fold transition is shown.

rendering.reason: Exterior standing study only. No measured balance, ground pressure, grasping or physiological simulation.

behaviors.label: Standing head turns
behaviors.description: A supported adult turns its head sideways, returns forward, turns the other way, then settles forward. The existing folded-wing exterior, feather textures and planted feet are retained. Two upper-neck controls distribute an illustrative 40-degree turn while the head surface moves together. The eight-second viewing sequence and transition curves are authored, not recorded bald-eagle movement or a universal scanning rate. This is an exterior posture study; eye movement, retinal vision, prey detection and muscle physiology are not simulated.
behaviors.evidence: Primary head-position observations; authored exterior articulation
behaviors.timeScale: Eight-second illustrative viewing interval; uncalibrated behavioral timing

rendering.reason: Finite supported head-turn sequence implemented on the separate standing exterior. Cervical vertebrae, measured joint trajectories, eye movements, visual fields, prey detection, rest physiology and capture mechanics are not modeled. Independent biological validation remains outstanding.

before.summary: A flightless diving bird. Breeding on sea ice and cooperative huddling help it persist in a cold environment.

anatomy.name: Flippers
anatomy.description: Source feathered flippers have smoothly bound shoulders. Left and right flippers stroke together dorsoventrally underwater; the outer blades stay stiff. Angle and amplitude are authored.

anatomy.name: Adult plumage
anatomy.description: The selected artist feather images are retained. Shorter bill and flipper proportions, paler yellow vertex-color adjustments and a pink lower-bill panel adapt its king-like traits toward an emperor exterior. This is an artist interpretation, not a measured live-animal morphometric fit.

anatomy.name: Feet and support
anatomy.description: The selected source retains two webbed feet, claws and short visible tarsi. Feet alternate support on land and trail while swimming; they are not the main propulsors. No display ground is included.

behaviors.label: Walk
behaviors.description: Four short alternating steps with the stance foot held in world space and a modest side-to-side shift. Both feet remain attached beneath the plumage and end supported. Step size, roll and timing are authored; no measured contact forces or gait speed is implied.
behaviors.evidence: Species-level scientific context; authored exterior posture study
behaviors.timeScale: uncalibrated illustrative display seconds; no biological clock

rendering.reason: Research-informed external articulation; not full physiology, fluid dynamics or independently validated kinematics.

behaviors.label: Swim
behaviors.description: Paired shoulder-driven flipper strokes on a streamlined belly-down exterior, both feet trailing. Active cycles use 1.47 Hz, the mean dominant cycle frequency from nine free-ranging emperor penguins in Sato et al. 2010. The authored eight-second demonstration settles into a glide; angles, amplitude and translational speed are not fitted to tracked animals.
behaviors.evidence: Species-level scientific context; authored exterior posture study
behaviors.timeScale: uncalibrated sequence timing; active cycle 1.47 Hz referenced to one emperor field dataset

sources.scope: Table 2: mean dominant stroke cycle frequency 1.47 Hz in nine free-ranging emperors; 1.35 Hz in a separate seven-bird Penguin Ranch dataset. Only the active cycle frequency is borrowed; no universal frequency, joint angles or swimming speed is claimed.

visual.fidelity: Uses the user-selected Marcel Porsiel exterior and its original feather images and UVs. Adds a bound seven-joint skeleton, continuous streamlined water posture, shorter bill and flippers, pink lower-bill and paler yellow vertex-color corrections. Two webbed feet remain visible. Walking uses alternating planted support; swimming uses paired stiff-flipper strokes followed by a glide. No display ground.

viewerRig.scope: Qualitative locomotion; 1.47 Hz active cycle referenced to Sato et al. 2010 table 2. No calibrated speed, thrust, energetics, thermoregulation or complete physiology.
viewerRig.description: Selected Marcel Porsiel feathered exterior with a new bound rig. Choose Walk or Swim to play the movement study. Swimming straightens the body and neck, keeps the belly down and trails both feet; paired flippers settle into a glide. Active stroke cycle: 1.47 Hz from an emperor field study; joint angles and step timing are authored.
